requirements.note: Inset-grouped main screen with Today (25) and All (135) smart lists and six coloured lists with open counts; counts update after completing, adding, deleting and reopening.

Open tasks come first, then a collapsible 'Completed (7)' header with a chevron. Tapping the circle completes a task (orange check) or reopens it, and the task goes back to its place in the open list.
Native sheet with title, notes, list picker, a pushed Priority picker and a due-date switch with an inline calendar. Tapping a row opens Edit Task and saving updates it.
Overdue dates are red with an alert icon and 'Overdue'. High priority shows an orange '!!!', low priority a '!'.
Swipe left shows a native iOS 27 Delete action, which works. Reordering works with system grips, but only after More > Edit Tasks; the order persists.

Rename (More > Rename List alert) and delete (More > Delete List, with a confirmation giving the task count; also Edit mode) both work and persist. Creating a list never works: the 'New List' alert accepts a name and Create closes it, but no list appears, not even after relaunch or in the task form's list picker. Tried four times.
Completions, the added and edited task, deletion, reordering, the rename and the list deletion all survived relaunch.

bugs: Add List > enter a name > Create does nothing: no list is created, and nothing appears after relaunch or in the list picker.
Renaming a list leaves it in its old slot ('Office' stays after 'Trip'), although the lists otherwise look alphabetical.
tells: Reordering needs a hidden More > Edit Tasks mode; there is no direct long-press drag.
'Add List' is a floating capsule in the bottom toolbar, and at the largest text size it overlaps list rows.
Low priority shows a bare '!' before the title, which reads like punctuation.
A.scroll: A native table: slow drags, flings and the return to the top were smooth, with no blank rows or jumps, and the large title collapses as it should.

requirements.note: 'Lists' screen with Today (25) and All (135) plus six lists with open counts, and a footer hint. Counts update correctly.
Open tasks, then a 'Completed · 7' row with a Show/Hide text button. The checkbox completes and reopens, and a reopened task returns to its original position. Expanded/collapsed resets on relaunch.
Native form sheet with title, a due-date switch plus a compact date picker, a priority pop-up menu and notes. Tapping a task opens Details for editing and saving works.
Overdue tasks show a red 'Overdue · date' with an alert icon. High priority gets an orange 'High' pill.
Swipe left reveals a red Delete pill, which works. Drag grips on every row reorder directly, and the order persists.
Create (New List sheet), rename (long press or the list's actions menu) and swipe-to-delete with a confirmation all work and persist.
All task and list changes survived relaunch.

tells: The task list screens don't look like UITableView/List: rows show up in the accessibility tree as web-style 'Link' elements in a plain scroll view, which hints at a non-native list.
Separators are inconsistent: there is a hairline above the first row, rows with a 'High' pill get a separator at a different inset, and one separator went missing after a pull at the top of All.
Swipe-to-delete is a custom red 'Delete' pill rather than the system swipe action.
Every list shows the same orange hamburger icon, which looks like a drag handle, and the lists have no colours.
Drag grips are always visible on every row, unlike iOS (normally shown only in edit mode).
The completed section uses a 'Show'/'Hide' text link instead of a disclosure chevron header.
At the largest text size, main-screen rows have almost no vertical padding and text crowds the separators.
B.scroll: Scrolling is smooth with momentum and rubber-banding, and no blank rows or pop-in were seen. There are minor separator glitches, and the rows don't quite feel like native table cells.

why: B does every requirement, including creating lists, which in A silently fails, so a core spec item is broken in A. A is the more convincing native app (system swipe actions, inset-grouped table, coloured list icons), while B's task lists show web-like structure and separator glitches. For shipping, a working feature set outweighs A's better polish.
